topic: Law of Chemical Equilibrium and Equilibrium Constant
title: The Equilibrium Constant Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Bake a cake with two eggs or four and the cake changes. Mix hydrogen and iodine in any amounts and, at one temperature, one number always comes out the same. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Diya doubles a tea recipe in her kitchen, and we find the rule behind every equilibrium mixture.

You will see three flasks on the molecule bench start with different amounts and reach different equilibrium mixtures, yet [HI] squared over [H2][I2] gives about 50.3 every time, while the plain ratio does not. We build the law of mass action (Guldberg and Waage, 1864) and the Kc expression step by step, then show what happens to Kc when you reverse, halve or double an equation, using Kc = 54.8 at 700 K. Then why only temperature changes Kc, a worked example, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 60 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
